ORIGINAL USMLE-STYLE PRACTICE

Granular debris in a granuloma

A patient with culture-confirmed tuberculosis undergoes lymph-node biopsy. The specimen contains epithelioid macrophages surrounding a central amorphous granular region with little recognizable tissue architecture. Which gross appearance would best correspond to this central necrotic material?

  1. Translucent mucin-filled spaces
  2. Dark red fibrin confined to a vessel wall
  3. Soft, friable, cheese-like material
  4. Firm pale tissue with preserved organ outlines
  5. Chalky white deposits in adipose tissue
Answer and explanation

Soft, friable, cheese-like material

Caseous necrosis has a characteristic cheese-like gross appearance and granular acellular debris microscopically.

Option explanations

Soft, friable, cheese-like material: Caseous necrosis has a characteristic cheese-like gross appearance and granular acellular debris microscopically.

Firm pale tissue with preserved organ outlines: Preserved outlines favor coagulative necrosis.

Chalky white deposits in adipose tissue: Chalky deposits in fat suggest saponification.

Translucent mucin-filled spaces: Mucin spaces are not the characteristic center of a tuberculous granuloma.

Dark red fibrin confined to a vessel wall: Vessel-wall fibrin deposition does not describe caseation.
